errors.english: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar
errors.why: The example is of those (the lifters) who individually cannot lift the beam but can when assembled; the beam is what is lifted, not the agent, and there is no pillar.

fix.find: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar
fix.replace: those who individually lack the capacity to lift the beam

note: Generally faithful rendering of Śākyabuddhi's discussion of recognition and the whole; the beam-lifting example has its agents inverted.
Accurate translation of the Mahāyāna-authenticity argument, including the transmission lineage and the opponent's positions.

errors.english: the object that we is refuting
errors.why: The refuter is the disputant (rgol ba), not 'we'.

note: Difficult nigrahasthāna passage (apratibhā/ajñāna) rendered sensibly; one garbled agent.

errors.english: why the possessor and so forth are not the reason
errors.why: ldan pa / ldan pa can are the Vaiśeṣika reasons saṃyoga / saṃyogin (conjunction / the conjoined), not 'possession/possessor'; the error recurs throughout the side.

fix.find: why the possessor and so forth are not the reason
fix.replace: why the conjoined (saṃyogin) and so forth are not reasons

errors.why: The gloss says the lemma means '[its indicating] is not denied', i.e. it is conceded, not a refutation.

note: Argument structure mostly followed, but the key Vaiśeṣika term saṃyogin is systematically mistranslated as 'possessor'.

errors.english: If mind [note: original: སེམས་, citta] were the self [note: original: བདག་, ātman], it could not be the object of the view of self.
errors.why: The gloss says that (past/future) mind, taken as the self, is not the object of self-view; the English recasts it as a general hypothetical about mind.

note: Good rendering of Prajñākaramati on the three-times mind and the plantain simile.

errors.english: Then because it has been abandoned, no bad reputation arises.
errors.why: The Tibetan says ill repute arises for him (as moonlight fades at dawn); the English adds a negation, which also clashes with the simile.

errors.english: When it is born, one is no longer visible,
errors.why: When anger arises, (the good) is not seen, in parallel with 'when unarisen, virtue is seen'; it is not that the person becomes invisible.

note: Verse jātaka rendered readably, but two stanzas on anger are distorted.

errors.english: the causes and conditions for how beings change
errors.why: The phrase completes 'rnam par dag par 'gyur ba'i' from the previous side: the causes and conditions of beings' becoming purified, not of their 'change'.

note: Accurate sūtra quotation on causes of defilement and purification, dhyāna and the eight liberations.

errors.english: the text says it is not so, raising a doubt one or two words at page break
errors.why: 'one or two words at page break' is stray editorial matter not in the Tibetan; the phrase introduces the refutation of the doubt (continuing on the next side).

fix.find: the text says it is not so, raising a doubt one or two words at page break
fix.replace: the text says "it is not so," [refuting] the doubt

errors.english: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
errors.why: The commentator says that, in dependence on the relative word 'which' (yat), the correlative 'from that cause' is to be supplied; the English misreads gang gi sgra as 'whichever word'.

errors.english: One must infer this because a certain result is seen at all times.
errors.why: This sentence belongs to the anticipated objection introduced by 'but if the result', not to the author's own view.

note: Gist of the humors-and-passions debate is there, but grammatical glosses are misread, the objection is mis-segmented, and stray editorial text intrudes.

errors.english: even if one were to search through each individual atom
errors.why: Dignāga's argument is that when the atoms are removed one by one, the cognition with the pot's form no longer arises; 'search through' obscures the subtraction argument.

note: Sound rendering of the Ālambanaparīkṣā commentary on atoms and conventional existence.
Faithful rendering of the Nyāyapraveśa-commentary passage on the unestablished pseudo-reason and the Digambara tree example.
